title: Luminos Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for Luminos Health onboarding to Redwood. Covered goals, success criteria, timeline, security requirements (SOC2/SAML/KMS), dedicated vs hosted options, pilot scope (triage notes assistant), data residency and audit logging. Agreed next steps: share onboarding plan and security pack, schedule technical deep dive and benchmark, set up trial Dedicated capacity for pilot. Several open action items with owners and tentative due dates.
topics: Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
next_steps: Redwood to send onboarding plan + security pack (SOC2, ISO docs, KMS whitepaper)
Schedule technical deep dive with Luminos infra team (Diego lead)
Redwood to provision trial Dedicated capacity for pilot (Clara to coordinate)
Customer to share sample anonymized data and primary triage workflows
action_items: Maya Patel - Send onboarding plan, pricing tiers, and pilot checklist - 2027-01-12
Diego Ramos - Schedule deep dive and propose benchmark tests (latency/cost) - 2027-01-14
Clara Nguyen - Provision trial Dedicated environment and invite Luminos SSO team - 2027-01-18
Jared Collins - Provide sample FHIR-derived anonymized data and triage prompts - 2027-01-13
Tom Ellis - Share security questionnaire answers and KMS requirements - 2027-01-15
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-10 15:00 PST
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Clara (Redwood CSM), Jared (Luminos Eng), Priya (PM), Tom (Security), Rosa (Clinical Ops)

00:00:03 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
00:00:07 Jared: yeah loud and clear, thanks Maya.
00:00:10 Maya: cool quick intros then i'll hand over to diego for tech stuff and clara on timeline, i'm maya i'll be your AE and point person on contract/pricing.
00:00:20 Priya: i'm priya product, i'm leading the triage assistant feature set.
00:00:24 Tom: tom here security architect, i'll be focused on compliance and KMS stuff.
00:00:29 Rosa: rosa from clinical ops, i'll help validate workflows and safety.
00:00:33 Diego: diego, solutions engineer, i'll run tech deep dives and benchmarks.
00:00:37 Clara: clara, customer success manager, i'll coordinate onboarding and the pilot.

00:01:05 Maya: high level - Luminos wants to add an LLM-powered triage notes assistant to improve scribe efficiency and reduce turnaround, success metric is 30% reduction in manual edit time and 99% uptime for core triage flows. correct?
00:01:22 Priya: yeah that's the primary goal, plus tight latency under 500ms ideally for interactive flows.
00:01:29 Jared: cause physicians need near real-time suggestions, anything >1s starts to feel laggy.

00:01:55 Diego: ok re infra, do you have a preferred hosting mode - hosted Redwood API, Dedicated reserved capacity, or private VPC/on-prem? we recommend Dedicated for predictable latency and data isolation but hosted is faster to get started.
00:02:14 Tom: For PHI concerns we are constrained - we need audit logs, encryption at rest with KMS integration, and SOC2 evidence. Private might be preferred, but if Dedicated with proper KMS and VPC peering is possible that could work.
00:02:33 Maya: totally, we see that pattern. for most health customers, Dedicated with customer-managed KMS and VPC peering hits the compliance checkboxes and still gives high throughput.
00:02:44 Diego: also note - the runtime supports KV cache and batching which helps lower per-token cost; we can tune quantization for the pilot to balance cost vs quality.
00:02:59 Priya: can you re-explain the KV cache? transcription flagged it as something else the other day.
00:03:05 Diego: sure, KV cache is basically the per-session key-value cache to avoid repeating earlier tokens during generation, reduces compute and latency for follow ups. sometimes the transcripter calls it K-V cash or key value catch - common.

00:03:40 Tom: SSO is important too, we use SAML2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. we need RBAC and audit trails in the console.
00:03:51 Clara: we support SAML and SCIM; console has token-level usage and audit logs. i'll include screenshots in the pack.

00:04:20 Rosa: workflow question - we want the model to redact PHI automatically and keep a human-in-the-loop change log. is that supported?
00:04:30 Diego: we don't do automatic PII removal out of the box but you can chain a text transformation step before passing to model. we also support structured output with tool-calling and constrained generation to help with safe redaction.

00:05:15 Priya: timeline - we want pilot live in 6-8 weeks with 2 clinics. is that realistic?
00:05:23 Clara: 6-8 weeks is tight but doable. typical flow: 1) share data/requirements 2) provision environment 3) integrate API + SSO 4) run benchmarks and model tuning 5) pilot validation. we'll aim for 6 weeks if we get sample data this week.

00:06:05 Jared: benchmark request - we need latency and cost per 1k tokens for our average triage prompt (we'll share examples).
00:06:12 Diego: we'll run a benchmark matrix across model variants and quantization profiles; propose a small test harness, we'll share results in a spreadsheet.

00:06:45 Tom: encryption - we need customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). is that available on Dedicated?
00:06:52 Maya: yes Dedicated supports bringing your own KMS; Private has the same option. i'll include the KMS integration guide.

00:07:25 Rosa: clinical validation - we need to produce a QA set and acceptance criteria; who owns that?
00:07:33 Priya: product will own acceptance criteria but we need Redwood's help on evals.
00:07:37 Diego: we have a quality monitoring and evals toolkit; we can run regression alerts tied to your prompt sets and compare model outputs across rollouts.

00:08:15 Priya: question about fallback behavior - if Dedicated capacity is saturated what's the graceful fallback?
00:08:23 Maya: we support routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants or hosted tier if you allow it; can configure per-route SLOs.
00:08:35 Jared: be explicit about cost tradeoffs if fallback goes to hosted.
00:08:38 Maya: noted, will include cost delta in the pilot pricing doc.

00:09:10 Diego: integration notes - API is REST/SDK, streaming responses supported, function/tool calls for structured outputs, and we expose token-level telemetry for debugging.
00:09:23 Priya: we plan to integrate via the Node SDK in our microservice. any gotchas?
00:09:27 Diego: the SDK handles streaming, but watch for connection limits; we'll share SDK best practices for connection pooling and batching.

00:10:02 Tom: also need to confirm data residency - some data must remain in us-east-1. can Dedicated be pinned by region?
00:10:09 Maya: yes region pinning is supported on Dedicated and Private.

00:10:35 Priya: ok pilot scope: start with triage notes assistant for 2 clinics, sample size ~2k encounters, focus on draft generation and edit-time reduction.
00:10:46 Diego: noted. for model selection i recommend starting with our verified Llama-variant and iterate; if you want smaller latency we can try a quantized variant.

00:11:30 Rosa: safety - we need a human override and a confidence flag on each suggestion.
00:11:36 Diego: we can include a confidence heuristic in the response metadata; the UI team can surface it.

00:12:10 Priya: what's the expected cost runway for pilot? we have a small budget - want to estimate per-encounter cost.
00:12:18 Maya: we'll send pilot pricing scenarios (hosted vs dedicated, batching assumptions). Clara will coordinate an estimate.

00:12:47 Jared: procurement timeline - we'll need a PO within a month after pilot approval.
00:12:53 Maya: okay noted.

00:13:20 Diego: let's talk about benchmark cadence - we'll run an initial smoke test, then a full latency/cost sweep and sample quality evals with your QA set.
00:13:31 Priya: sample prompts and acceptance cases will be shared by EoD Thursday.
00:13:36 Jared: yes we'll try to get them by Thursday.

00:14:05 Tom: security questionnaire - can you share your standard security pack and SOC2 type II evidence?
00:14:12 Maya: yes will include the security pack link; note some items require NDA for deeper docs.
00:14:19 Tom: we can sign an NDA.

00:15:00 Clara: summary of next steps: maya send onboarding + security pack, diego schedule deep dive and benchmark, clara provision trial dedicated env, customer share data and prompts.
00:15:12 Priya: one more question - model versioning and rollouts: can we pin model versions per environment?
00:15:20 Diego: yes you can pin versions and do canary/A-B rollouts with automatic rollback on regression alerts.

00:15:45 Rosa: testing - will Redwood run an initial red-team for hallucination checks?
00:15:51 Diego: we don't do red-team by default but we can assist with adversarial prompt sets during eval.

00:16:30 Priya: any regulatory concerns for PHI annotation?
00:16:36 Tom: we will need data de-identification steps; legal will sign off.

00:17:00 Maya: okay i'll recap then we'll open for questions.
00:17:05 Priya: nothing else from product.
00:17:09 Jared: quick one - will logs include raw content or hashed tokens? we want minimal exposure.
00:17:15 Diego: logs can be configured; for Dedicated you can restrict raw logs and send hashed or redacted versions to the console.
00:17:30 Tom: good.

00:18:00 Maya: any blockers to start the 6-week plan?
00:18:05 Jared: the main blocker is getting the anonymized samples and security questionnaire answers.
00:18:10 Tom: and KMS details for key provisioning.
00:18:14 Clara: we'll follow up with a calendar poll for the deep dive.

00:19:00 Priya: ok thanks everyone.
00:19:05 Maya: thanks all, we'll send the pack and follow up items.
00:19:09 Diego: i'll email proposed benchmark matrix post-call.
00:19:13 Clara: i'll create the trial env and invite Tom's team to the SSO test.
00:19:20 Rosa: thanks.
00:19:24 [call ends - small talk and hangups]

Note: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., KV cache sometimes "K-V cash"), speaker labels simplified, and occasional run-on sentences as typical of automated meeting transcripts.
references: Benchmark spreadsheet (will be shared by Diego post-call)
